A QUICK START

Less setup.
More playing.

Try it without a guitar

Click Test riff and choose a factory preset. The source is a synthesized plucked-string loop. Adjust sliders, engage pedals with their footswitches, and reorder with the arrows.

Connect a guitar

  1. Connect your guitar to a USB interface's instrument / Hi-Z input.
  2. Connect wired headphones to the interface, choose it as your system output, and turn direct monitoring off.
  3. Start with low headphone gain. Click Start audio, then Connect guitar and allow microphone access. This permission includes USB audio interfaces.
  4. Select the interface and reconnect if you change devices. Choose Channel 1 or 2 to match the instrument input.
  5. Play and adjust interface gain to avoid clipping. Use input trim and master volume for fine adjustments.

No live input is uploaded. HTTPS or localhost is required. Device names can stay hidden until input access is allowed. Output uses your system default device.

Find your sound

EffectStarting point
GateThreshold just above idle noise; longer Release to preserve note tails.
Compressor3:1 ratio for gentle control. Match loudness with Makeup.
OverdriveRaise Drive for saturation, lower Level to match bypass volume.
EQAdjust low/high shelves and sweep the parametric mid frequency.
ChorusSlow Rate and 25% Mix for gentle movement.
Delay100 ms slapback, 375 ms longer repeats. Feedback controls the tail.
ReverbLow Mix for a room; raise Decay and Mix for ambient washes.
CabinetUpload a short cabinet WAV. Default is a synthetic filter.

The tuner listens before effects. Play one string at a time. Mute output to tune silently. Global bypass skips pedals while retaining trim and master volume.

Save a tone

Enter a name and click Save preset. Reusing a name updates it. Sounds and IRs persist in this browser. Export JSON for a backup including the custom IR. Import applies a sound; Save preset keeps it. Device, channel, global bypass and tuner mute are session controls.

Reusable effects API

import { createEffect, Pedalboard } from './src/pedalboard.js';

// Use your DAW's existing AudioContext:
await context.resume();
const drive = await createEffect(context, 'overdrive', {
  params: { drive: 30, tone: 3500, level: -12 }
});
source.connect(drive.input);
drive.connect(trackMixer);
drive.setParam('drive', 45);
drive.setEnabled(false);
// When removing an effect:
drive.dispose();

const board = await Pedalboard.create(context);
source.connect(board.input);
board.output.connect(trackMixer);
const preset = board.serialize();
board.applyPreset(preset);

Independent classes: NoiseGate, Compressor, Overdrive, Equalizer, Chorus, Delay, Reverb, Cabinet. All expose input, output, setParam, configure, setEnabled, serialize and dispose. EFFECTS exports ranges and defaults. Use createEffect for automatic gate worklet registration.

const cab = await createEffect(context, 'cabinet');
await cab.loadIR(await file.arrayBuffer(), {
  name: file.name, id: 'my-cabinet'
});

The library serializes an IR reference. Your host stores/resolves that audio asset separately; the demo uses IndexedDB and embeds the IR when exporting JSON. The included README describes the complete API.

V1 limits

The default cabinet is synthetic. No amp model or VST/AU hosting is included. IR gain is preserved and there is no hard limiter: reduce volume before loading unfamiliar IRs or boosting heavily. Cabinet files must decode as mono/stereo and be at most 5 seconds / 5 MB.

Reported output latency excludes capture latency. Test the actual interface before live use. The monophonic tuner covers 65–1400 Hz. Reordering can click during sustained notes, and decay edits can interrupt reverb tails. Bypassed effects keep running internally.
